claims.text: Intervention X causes a 20% improvement in outcome Y.

evidence_anchors.quote_or_fact: A single observational cohort of 80 participants received intervention X. There was no randomized control group.

tasks.objective: Audit identification of the causal claim

concerns.title: The design does not identify the headline causal effect
concerns.failure_mechanism: A single-group pre-post comparison has no concurrent counterfactual and cannot separate intervention effects from time trends, regression to the mean, co-interventions, or other changes.
concerns.scientific_consequence: The evidence can support a within-cohort pre-post association but not the stated causal conclusion.
concerns.minimum_resolution: Reframe the central conclusion as associational unless a design or analysis that credibly identifies the treatment effect is available.
concerns.closure_criterion: The title/abstract/conclusion no longer make a causal claim, or a defensible identification strategy with appropriate comparison data is demonstrated.

concern_verifier:M001.rationale: The cited methods anchor directly establishes the absence of a concurrent control group, and the concern is limited to causal identification rather than denying the observed pre-post change.

claim_evidence_alignment.reason: The central causal claim exceeds what the design identifies.

decision_brief.central_scientific_issue: The observed pre-post change is not sufficient to identify a causal treatment effect.

strengths: The numerical pre-post result is stated clearly.
limitations: Causal identification is the decisive limitation.
